claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a random solid solution.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has significant atomic-size mismatch and local lattice distortion.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations in random HfNbTaTiZr cause strong phonon scattering and low lattice thermal conductivity.
Monte Carlo equilibration can induce chemical short-range order in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Monte Carlo treatment of HfNbTaTiZr produces HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The HfTi and TiZr clusters undergo a percolative transition into B2-like superstructures.
B2-like ordering reduces RMS atomic displacements and local lattice strain relative to random HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced local distortion lowers the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
The random alloy is in a mass-disorder-dominated high-frequency phonon-scattering regime.
Periodicity in the B2-like clusters restores high-frequency phonon coherence.
Percolating SRO clusters create continuous pathways along which phonons propagate with reduced scattering times.
The reduction in distortion scattering outweighs scattering introduced by ordering and therefore increases lattice thermal conductivity.
The relevant high-frequency modes are above 10 THz.
Ordering will increase lattice thermal conductivity by 15–25% relative to the random state between 300 K and 800 K.
The ordered state will exhibit sharper high-frequency phonon-DOS peaks due to reduced scattering.
Atomic displacement amplitudes in ordered regions will be 10–15% lower than in the random solid solution.
A conductivity increase requires both a percolating ordered network and a significant reduction in lattice distortion.
Discrete precipitates or highly strained ordered-phase interfaces will instead reduce conductivity through interface scattering.
Low-frequency phonons may remain strongly scattered by cluster boundaries even when high-frequency transport improves.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes higher conductivity to weaker scattering, but the mechanism says phonons propagate with reduced scattering times τ. In the usual kinetic relation, weaker scattering corresponds to a longer relaxation time, whereas a reduced τ would lower conductivity. The intended phrase may have been reduced scattering rates.
